title: Lunch, at the speed of imagination.
summary: Meet Burrito Blaster: an entirely fictional delivery simulation that prepares an order, checks its destination, simulates a burrito launch, and records the outcome. All the excitement of a mission-control dashboard, with none of the real-world projectiles.
source_note: Fictional demonstration. No real orders, coordinates, projectiles, or messages are used.
panel_body: An order goes in. A clearly labeled simulated result comes out. Every branch remains visible, even when the mission must pause.

highlights.title: Wrap with purpose
highlights.description: Check the imaginary order and pack a fictional burrito before anything moves.

highlights.title: Know the destination
highlights.description: Only a destination verified in the simulated data can proceed to launch.

highlights.title: Never fake the landing
highlights.description: Confirm or pause the mission based on the simulated outcome, then record the result.

flow.title: The extraordinary journey of an ordinary burrito
flow.description: Follow the main example path, or select a declared detour to see what happens when an order, ingredient, destination, landing, or notification cannot be confirmed. This is a clickable explanation, not a real launcher.

nodes.title: Check the order
nodes.summary: Is there enough fictional order data to start?
nodes.detail: Validate the imaginary order reference and customer details. Without a usable order, halt the simulation at Pause rather than pretending one exists.

nodes.title: Wrap the burrito
nodes.summary: Prepare the fictional meal and check ingredients.
nodes.detail: Assemble the requested pretend burrito. If an ingredient requirement cannot be met, use Stop. Successful preparation yields a wrapped demo burrito reference.

nodes.title: Verify destination
nodes.summary: Resolve the destination using simulated customer data.
nodes.detail: Read a mock address and fictional coordinates. Only verified simulated coordinates unlock the next step; unknown or ambiguous destinations lead to Pause.

nodes.title: Simulate the launch
nodes.summary: Pretend to fire the cannon; record an imagined landing.
nodes.detail: Run a simulation of burrito delivery. No mechanical device is controlled and nothing is launched. If the fictional landing cannot be confirmed, route to Pause.

nodes.title: Record notification
nodes.summary: Simulate a message or explicitly skip it.
nodes.detail: Record the fictional notification outcome; do not send an actual SMS. If the simulated messaging path is unavailable, route to Pause.

nodes.title: Complete the demo
nodes.summary: Return the simulated order, delivery, and notification outcomes.
nodes.detail: The example finishes with a burrito reference, a verified simulated destination, delivery result, and notification result. Completion reflects only the fictional demonstration.

nodes.title: Pause for clarity
nodes.summary: Stop progressing until uncertain inputs or results are resolved.
nodes.detail: Preserve the partial demo result and explain which fictional input, destination, landing, or notification remains uncertain. The preview does not restart the mission on its own.

nodes.title: Stop the attempt
nodes.summary: Record a terminal issue with the pretend order.
nodes.detail: End this simulated delivery attempt if an ingredient requirement fails. Record what happened instead of pretending the burrito was prepared.

chapters.title: A lunch break with mission control
chapters.body: Burrito Blaster turns a very ordinary task into an intentionally ridiculous systems demo. The storytelling is playful; the underlying sequence and decisions stay exact.
points: Start with an order and a prepared burrito
Verify the fictional destination before any simulated launch
Show both success and uncertainty honestly

chapters.title: There is no actual cannon
chapters.body: Every operational detail is simulated. This is a human-readable walkthrough—not a dispatch system, customer lookup, SMS sender, or physical launcher.
points: Never represent sample coordinates as a real location
Never imply a real notification was delivered
Never hide pause or stop branches

chapters.title: Every path should tell the truth
chapters.body: Good explanations have visible conditions and honest endings. The same story can be dressed as polished product engineering, a cheerful retro game, or an ornate fantasy briefing without changing the facts.
points: Primary route: six stages, from order check to completion
Alternate routes: pause or stop with a visible reason
Presentation controls explore the example; they do not execute it

callouts.title: Only a preview—not a real launch
callouts.text: Every order, destination, launch, and notification in this example is simulated.

callouts.title: What if the destination is unknown?
callouts.text: The declared route pauses rather than pretending an address or delivery result was confirmed.
